summary: Hu Jintao arrived in London at the start of a European tour, with visits to France, Germany, and Spain to follow.
During his British tour, Chinese Vice-President Hu Jintao asked the prime minister to support China's struggle against its domestic terrorists.
Vice-President Hu Jintao, seen as the man most likely to succeed President Jiang Zemin as party leader, started a European tour by visiting Moscow and London.
Hu Jintao is expected to succeed Jiang Zemin as party general secretary as the party congress clears the way for China's new leadership.
Hu Jintao is expected to become China's leader.
Hu Jintao takes over as Communist Party general secretary from Jiang Zemin, who resigns but stays on as chairman of the military commission.
Hu Jintao was appointed general secretary of the Communist Party of China, clearing the way for him to assume full power when Jiang Zemin stands down as Chinese president in March.
Hu Jintao, newly appointed Communist party leader, revived Mao Zedong's call for "plain living and hard struggle" in a speech during his visit to the revolutionary base of Xibaibo.
Hu Jintao's keynote speech urging party members to live simply and resist corruption was published on the front pages of major Chinese newspapers, after being delivered on 2002-12-06.
China's parliament elected Hu Jintao as president, while outgoing president Jiang Zemin retained his post as head of the central military commission despite precedent that it should go to Hu.
The new government of President Hu Jintao issued an edict against compulsory subscriptions that previously provided Chinese publications' main source of income.
China's president Hu Jintao rejected a personal appeal from US President George Bush to revalue China's currency and adjust other trade policies during a summit of Pacific rim leaders in Bangkok.
Chinese President Hu Jintao supported George Bush's push to prioritize the war on terror at the APEC summit in Bangkok, urging closer cooperation to combat terrorism.
Hu Jintao assumed the chairmanship of China's central military commission.
Speculation grows that Jiang Zemin may resign as chairman of the central military commission, potentially ceding his last position of authority to Hu Jintao.
Jiang Zemin is reported to have resigned as head of the People's Liberation Army, with President Hu Jintao expected to replace him as chief of the military.
Hu Jintao assumes the party's military commandership after Jiang Zemin's resignation from the Central Military Commission, strengthening his status as the core of a new-generation leadership.
President Hu Jintao joins dozens of African and Asian leaders at a celebratory summit in Indonesia marking the 50th anniversary of the Bandung conference.

Taiwanese opposition leader Lien Chan and Chinese President Hu Jintao held a historic meeting in Beijing, the highest-level talks since 1949, and issued a joint statement promising to work together to try to end hostilities between Beijing and Taipei.
Hu Jintao called for a "smokeless war" against "liberal elements" during a secret leadership meeting, according to a New York Times report.

Under Hu Jintao, China intensified internet censorship, including a filter system triggered by words such as "democracy" and a requirement for websites and weblogs to register with real names and identity numbers.
The Communist Youth League, the power base of President Hu Jintao, sponsors the development of an online game titled "Anti-Japan War Online" to foster patriotism among young internet users.
Chinese President Hu Jintao arrives in central London for a three-day state visit, greeted by a royal reception and protests from pro-Tibet and democracy activists.
Tony Blair held talks with Chinese President Hu Jintao in Downing Street, where noisy protests took place outside.
A letter from the Chinese Embassy rejects as groundless an allegation that many members of President Hu Jintao's entourage were left in the UK as espionage agents.

China's leadership, in a decision attributed to President Hu Jintao, announces it will hold a memorial marking the 90th anniversary of former party chief Hu Yaobang's birth, with reports suggesting a ceremony in Beijing on November 18 that Hu Jintao will not attend.
Chinese journalist Jiang Weiping was released from jail ahead of a planned trip to the US by Chinese President Hu Jintao.
Chinese President Hu Jintao begins a visit to the US, starting with a Boeing plant in Seattle and a dinner at Bill Gates's home, aimed at showing China is a responsible stakeholder and not a threat.
Hu Jintao's visit to Washington was disrupted by a Falun Gong protester during his speech at the White House, and no progress was made with President Bush on trade, North Korea, or Iran.

President Hu Jintao visited Washington for meetings with George Bush, during which a Chinese journalist disrupted the White House lawn ceremony with a protest about Falun Gong persecution and human rights abuses.
Chinese President Hu Jintao visits the United States, receiving a 21-gun salute at the White House and a dinner at Bill Gates's house, with protesters present throughout his visit.
Chinese President Hu Jintao visits Africa to strengthen economic ties and secure natural resources, emphasizing non-interference in human rights.
Chinese President Hu Jintao hosts a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit of 10 nations in Shanghai, promoting peace and stability in a region increasingly important for oil and gas.

President Hu Jintao hailed the opening of the Qinghai-Tibet railway and dismissed criticism of China's Tibet policies as imperialist media mischief, claiming China is ambitious, confident, and capable of standing among advanced nations.
Human rights groups reported that at least 100 dissidents in Beijing had been jailed, beaten or placed under house arrest since mid-August under the leadership of Hu Jintao and Wen Jiabao.

Shanghai Communist party chief Chen Liangyu was fired in China's highest-level corruption scandal in over 10 years, signaling an escalation of a purge by President Hu Jintao as he tightens his grip on power.
Shanghai Communist party chief Chen Liangyu was fired and placed under criminal investigation in a corruption scandal, signaling an escalation of President Hu Jintao's purge of regional leaders.
Hu Jintao detained Shanghai party boss Chen Liangyu on corruption charges, in a move seen as an attempt to bolster central authority ahead of the next year's party congress.
Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe visits China for talks with President Hu Jintao, in an attempt to repair damaged bilateral relations.
Hu Jintao begins an 11-day tour of Africa, starting with Cameroon, and announces $3bn in credit, additional aid, and interest-free loans to African countries.
US President George Bush and Chinese President Hu Jintao held a rare face-to-face meeting at the Apec summit in Sydney, discussing product safety, trade imbalances, political freedoms, and Taiwan.
The 17th congress of the Chinese Communist party begins in Beijing, where delegates will eventually choose a successor to Hu Jintao.

President Hu Jintao, in a speech at the Communist Party's 17th congress, said that under his leadership China's overall strength grew considerably and people enjoyed more tangible benefits, while acknowledging "unprecedented challenges."
President Hu Jintao opened the 17th Communist Party congress in Beijing, calling for power to be exercised "in the sunshine" and envisaging expanded "inner party democracy."

Hu Jintao is expected to secure a second term as party leader at the Chinese Communist party congress, though his authority is reportedly constrained by factionalism and his chosen successor may not be elevated as planned.

Hu Jintao secured a second five-year term as Chinese president and strengthened his authority after his rival Zeng Qinghong lost his place on the party's central committee at the close of the 17th party congress.

At the 17th party congress, Hu Jintao secured his second five-year term as party leader and had his "scientific development" concept written into the party charter, while Xi Jinping and Li Keqiang were promoted to the politburo standing committee.
The Dalai Lama says he is willing to meet Chinese leaders, particularly President Hu Jintao, but will wait for concrete signs that the situation in Tibet is becoming more positive.
Chinese President Hu Jintao met Taiwan's vice-president-elect Vincent Siew on the sidelines of the Boao Forum for Asia, the highest-level contact between the two sides since 1949.
Chinese internet users launched an online campaign against Mianyang Communist Party chief Tan Li, accusing him of grinning while escorting President Hu Jintao around his town after the earthquake.
Hu Jintao arrives in Tokyo on the first visit to Japan by a Chinese president in a decade, aiming to improve Sino-Japanese ties.
Chinese President Hu Jintao accused the Dalai Lama of attempting to ruin the Beijing Olympics and challenged him to show sincerity in opposing violent resistance to Chinese rule in Tibet.

President Hu Jintao visited the earthquake-stricken town of Beichuan and appeared on state television reassuring the injured and spurring rescuers on, as the death toll from the 7.9-magnitude quake reached 28,881.
Zhang Shijun published an open letter to Chinese President Hu Jintao urging him to reassess the June 4 Tiananmen Square crackdown.
Hu Jintao attends the lavish ceremony at the new opera house in Beijing where the IOC's annual session is officially declared open.
Forty Olympic athletes, including world record holder Dayron Robles, sign a letter to Chinese President Hu Jintao calling for a peaceful solution in Tibet and respect for human rights.
Gordon Brown urged Chinese President Hu Jintao to extend media freedom beyond the Beijing Olympics during a meeting in Beijing.
Hu Jintao is leading a large Chinese business delegation through Latin America to strengthen Beijing's economic ties, launching free trade talks in Costa Rica and signing agreements in Cuba.
President Hu Jintao called for a "great wall" of stability in Tibet on the eve of the 50th anniversary of the failed anti-Chinese uprising that led to the Dalai Lama's exile.
At a G20 summit dinner hosted by Gordon Brown, Chinese President Hu Jintao sat to Brown's right, while Hu's first face-to-face meeting with Barack Obama was anticipated.
Hu Jintao met bilaterally with President Obama on the sidelines of the G20 summit, a meeting privately dubbed the G2.
Hu Jintao and Barack Obama received the main headlines from the UN climate change summit.
Barack Obama and Chinese president Hu Jintao held talks in Beijing, lauding increased co-operation while raising differences over Tibet, human rights, trade and Iran.
China's president Hu Jintao called for a clean-up of football, leading to a crackdown in which more than 20 sports officials were arrested for match-fixing and corruption.
Chinese foreign ministry says President Hu Jintao will visit Washington on 12-13 April for a nuclear proliferation summit.
Chinese President Hu Jintao flew into the earthquake-devastated town in Yushu county, Qinghai province, pledging swift rebuilding as the death toll reached 1,700.
Hu Jintao hosts world leaders at the opening of the Shanghai Expo 2010 amid intense security.
Hu Jintao is due to arrive in Washington for a four-day state visit, highlighted by a White House state dinner on Wednesday.

During his state visit to the US, Chinese President Hu Jintao publicly acknowledged for the first time that China still needs to improve its human rights record, after Barack Obama raised the issue twice in public.
Hu Jintao's state visit to Washington was lauded by Chinese state media, which downplayed remarks on human rights.

Chinese President Hu Jintao received a sceptical and hostile reception at the US Congress, where Republicans and Democrats attacked China's human rights record, alleged currency manipulation, and accused Beijing of bullying its neighbours.
Hu Jintao's state visit to the US draws criticism from conservative radio hosts over human rights and China's economic practices.
Chinese President Hu Jintao warned that the Communist Party faces corruption and other "growing pains" as it celebrated its 90th anniversary at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing.
Officials in Chongqing wiretapped a call to President Hu Jintao, an incident that helped trigger the investigation of Bo Xilai.
Barack Obama and Hu Jintao meet at a nuclear summit in Seoul.
Hu Jintao visited Hong Kong and swore in Leung Chun-ying as the new chief executive amid large protests.
Hu Jintao warned at the 18th party congress that corruption could cause the collapse of the party and the fall of the state, and called for safeguarding party control.

The Chinese Communist party concluded its 18th national congress, upgrading outgoing leader Hu Jintao's theoretical innovation, the scientific outlook on development, to rank alongside other guiding ideologies within the party constitution.
Hu Jintao is going to stand down from his military post, so that Xi Jinping will lead the party, the government and the military.
Chinese anti-corruption authorities place Ling Jihua, a top aide to former president Hu Jintao, under investigation for suspected serious disciplinary violation.

Xi Jinping is in the UK for the first state visit to Britain by a Chinese head of state in 10 years, a visit that reciprocates several made by Conservative politicians to China; Hu Jintao, Xi's predecessor, visited the country in 2005, when Tony Blair was prime minister.

China’s state prosecuting body announced that Ling Jihua, former top aide to then President Hu Jintao, will be tried in Tianjin on charges of taking massive bribes and illegally obtaining state secrets.

Hu Jintao delivered a speech at the 18th party congress warning the incoming generation of leaders not to change the system, emphasizing continuity with Mao Zedong thought and rejecting political pluralism.
The article discusses Hu Jintao and Wen Jiabao planning China's leadership succession, but no specific dated event is reported.
Chinese president Hu Jintao visits the US.

The World Association of Newspapers and World Editors Forum delivered a protest letter to Chinese President Hu Jintao over the jailing of two journalists and a crackdown on freedom of expression ahead of the Beijing Olympics.
Hu Jintao is expected to step down as President of China in autumn 2012, handing over to a successor in the first leadership transition not shaped by the founders of the People's Republic.
